name: emission-is-bounded-within-one-callback
note: ABI §9.7 rule 9: a host that publishes max_emission_bytes bounds the payload bytes it accepts from emit within one callback, and answers ERR_LIMIT past it. The block emits the same five-byte batch three times against a budget of twelve and checks the three answers itself (0, 0, ERR_LIMIT), returning -1, -2 or -3 to name whichever was wrong — so a status of 0 is the assertion. Two deliveries, because the second is the half a per-instance counter would fail: the budget is per callback, and ABI §6.2's routing-after-the-callback is what makes the drain the boundary. errors 0 pins that a refusal is a status code and not a death (§8), and the two emissions that did land are asserted so a host cannot pass by refusing all three.
